Both corrections are done, tested, and verified end-to-end. The updated build is ready at **http://maker:4000** (sign in with `review@example.com` / `review-access`; the broker serves the new code).

**What I fixed (both were implementation errors against approved behaviour, corrected within this cycle):**

1. **Page copies are now a single self-contained HTML file.** Capturing a normal page stores a complete HTML document with its **stylesheets and images inlined** and scripts removed, so it still renders if the original disappears. In the app, "View saved copy" now shows the preserved page itself (in a sandboxed frame, plus "Open in a new tab"). PDFs are still stored and served as the actual PDF.

2. **The JSON backup is now complete and restores everything.** Export includes each bookmark's **saved-copy content** (the page's HTML, or the PDF itself), its **Internet Archive reference**, tags, note, reading/archive state, and **both dates**. Importing that backup into another account restores all of it — I verified a full round-trip: a saved page and its dates came back intact and the preserved page was viewable after import. The browser-standard HTML export/import remains the flat, title+tags+date interchange format, and import still merges and skips duplicates.

**Verification:** all automated tests pass (16/16, now including a self-contained-HTML check and a full backup/restore round-trip), plus a live end-to-end run across two accounts.

Everything else we approved is unchanged from the previous report.
